cells.tense: The pen is in your hand now, and the declaration is yours to sign.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Take a sheet and set down every pull on you right now — the asks, the obligations, the wishes — then mark beside each whether it started with you. Not which ones to keep. Which began as your own.
cells.core:
Declaring what goes where comes easily to you — the sentence that sets a boundary, the plan that holds, the thing said plainly. You can take a mess and put a shape around it. That isn't force. It's focus. That's the thing that lands with people: they can feel where you've pointed.

What strong direction needs underneath it is knowing which pulls are yours. You've got plenty of voices in the mix, and most of them can wait. So before you declare the next thing, sort them. Which direction did you actually choose, and which one arrived already assembled. You can name what you're keeping and set the rest aside as borrowed. A direction you picked holds longer than one you inherited.
cells.sheetLine: Choose direction and know which pulls are yours.
cells.verb: claiming a place with a clear declaration
cells.place: at the point where direction is chosen and meant

cells.tense: The next move is already decided in your head, and the decision runs before the room.
cells.act: follow the thought past where it is comfortable
cells.ask: Take one of these pushes and follow it all the way down — past the spot where you'd normally settle on the answer — and keep going until you reach the edge of what you actually know. Stop only there.
cells.core:
You organize before you arrive. The framework for a decision gets drafted early, and by the time the room is in it, the structure is already up — charted, named, ready. A lot of people are grateful for that. It is also how a plan gets declared at 7 a.m. for a day that hasn't said what it is yet.

Pushing the plan further out doesn't make it truer. Going all the way into one thought until it meets its own limit does something else: it shows you where sharpness stops being knowledge. There's a point beyond the plan where you don't see the next thing, and that's not failure — that's the edge of what you can know. The pressure to declare lifts when you know where your own knowing ends. Then the declaration is a choice, not a flood.
cells.sheetLine: Your plans run before the room and decide before it speaks.

cells.tense: You stand at a threshold that has already closed behind you, waiting.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Choose something you've been circling for a while, and do the next small piece of it today, nothing more. Tomorrow, the piece after. Direction gets a floor under it that way, one day at a time.
cells.core:
Where you choose a direction and mean it, that's where you've gone quiet. There used to be a clear line from here is what you want to here is what you do, and lately the second half hasn't been showing up. Not lazy. Not indecisive. The place where choosing turns into motion just hasn't been getting charged.

Force won't restart it. Push harder and the empty engine floods. What does work is small, sustained craft — one piece a day, on something you picked once and didn't renegotiate every morning. Direction gets built the way walls do, one commitment thicker daily. After a week it will surprise you how much you meant.
cells.sheetLine: You're waiting at a threshold that has already closed.

cells.tense: You've been steering and living as if the steering happened on its own.
cells.ask: Name the two or three directions you actually steered last year — not the ones assigned, the ones you chose the shape of. Then look at what came back from putting your hand on them.
cells.core:
You point the room. Directions get set because of decisions you didn't stop to register as decisions — the project that exists because you said yes, the situation that cleared because you named it. You'd call it going that way. The people on the other side of it wouldn't.

So look back over what changed this year and name the steering as yours. Not a boast. An inventory. There's a room that only exists because you organized it, and there's a version of you that doesn't remember picking it. Gathering the yield is collecting what the choices already grew. Take what's yours off the shelf and put it where you can see it. Then the next choice starts from a full room.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering and have forgotten the wheel is in your hands.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that at Too Little the person is hiding behind an old door — the record only says the seat is starved, not what stands in the way or when it was built. A reader could object that they are tired and scattered rather than withdrawn, so the cell must let them say no and still hold something usable. The asks survive being wrong: each is an experiment in the seat itself, not a verdict, and none requires knowing the cause. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that explains why the capacity went quiet, so no cause is named — only the shape of the quiet and one small move.
